instagram.caption:
How to price a job: put 3 prices on every quote. For HVAC, plumbing and electrical business owners.
ServiceTitan data (12 months to Jan 2026): the top 10% of shops by revenue offered good, better, best on 57% of home jobs. Everyone else: 41%.

Quote Clinic, Lesson 4: build your three like this.
Good ($): the job done right. Nothing extra.
Better ($$): what you'd pick for your own house.
Best ($$$): plus upgrades, like a longer warranty or a faster start date.

Why the middle works: in 7 years of orders at a German restaurant, a dish that became the middle option gained about 5 points of share on average (Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization, 2016).
An ACCA survey of 1,000+ contractors: 4+ options closed 52% of the time, 1 to 3 options 42% (ACHR News, 2026). It groups 1 to 3 together, so it can't show 3 beats 1.

Send this to whoever writes your quotes.
One price or three on your quotes? Tell me what happens when you give three.

Narrated by an AI version of my own voice.

youtube.title: How to Price a Job: Put 3 Prices on Every Quote (HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical)
youtube.description:
How to price a job with good, better, best: put 3 prices on every quote. For HVAC, plumbing, electrical and home service business owners.
ServiceTitan, State of the Trades, Top Performer Profile: top performers (the 90th percentile of revenue in their trade and market) offered good, better, best proposals on 57% of residential jobs; everyone else on 41% (aggregated ServiceTitan customer data, trailing 12 months through January 2026).
Pinger, Ruhmer-Krell and Schumacher, "The compromise effect in action: Lessons from a restaurant's menu," Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization 128 (2016): 7 years of orders at a German restaurant; an option that became the middle choice gained on average 5 percentage points of share, more when the added option was at the high end.
ACCA and Farmington Consulting Group, "Contractor of the Future" survey of 1,000+ contractors (ACHR News, Feb 10, 2026): 4+ options closed 52% of the time; 1 to 3 options closed 42%. The survey groups 1, 2 and 3 options together, so it does not show that 3 beats 1.

Build your three:
1. Good ($): the job done right. Nothing extra.
2. Better ($$): what you'd pick for your own house.
3. Best ($$$): plus upgrades, like a longer warranty or a faster start date.

One price is a yes or a no. Three prices is a choice. Send this to whoever writes your quotes.
